takeaways: A January tour of a Key Land Homes two-story in Rosemount, on the southeast side of the metro, where local industry means it's more than a bedroom community.
Four bedrooms, four baths, just under 2,600 square feet and a three-car garage, priced around $700,000 at the time.

The standout is a main-floor bedroom suite with its own three-quarter bath, useful for guests or a family member staying long-term. The main floor also has a mini office, a stacked-stone fireplace prewired for a TV, a two-tone kitchen with a five-burner range and a mudroom with two benches.
Upstairs are a modest loft, laundry, two bedrooms sharing a bath with a separate door, and the owner's suite. Jason estimates finishing the basement at about $45,000 to $60,000.

faq.q: Are there new homes with a main-floor bedroom suite in Rosemount?
faq.a: Yes. This Key Land Homes two-story in Rosemount has a main-floor bedroom with its own three-quarter bath, plus three bedrooms upstairs.

takeaways: A tour of D.R. Horton's Jordan model at Rivertown Heights in Chaska, where 64 lots remained at the time.
About 3,000 square feet with five bedrooms and three baths, priced around $650,000 at the time. Finishing the walkout basement would add about 1,200 square feet for roughly $50,000 to $60,000.

The main floor has a dining room or office, a kitchen with double ovens and a large pantry, a living room with views out back and a bedroom with a full bath next to it. Homes come with smart-home controls.
Upstairs are a very large loft, laundry, three bedrooms sharing a bath and an owner's suite with two closets, a soaking tub and a three-quarter shower.

faq.q: What does about $650,000 buy in new construction in Chaska?
faq.a: In this tour, a D.R. Horton home of about 3,000 square feet with five bedrooms, three baths, a main-floor bedroom and an unfinished walkout basement.

takeaways: How to choose a real estate agent in the Twin Cities, where there are nearly 21,000 active agents in the 13-county metro.

Jason compared the area's top teams by Google review count and rating plus closed sales over 12 months. Five large teams stood out, Huerkamp Home Group among them with 730 five-star Google reviews at the time of recording.

Red flag 1: big promises without a track record. Look for 50-plus reviews on Google and Zillow. The average agent sells about five homes a year, according to Jason; agents on his team average about 17.
Red flag 2: little experience in your area or property type, whether new construction, land, lakeshore, golf communities or investment property. Zillow shows each agent's past sales on a map.

Red flag 3: weak marketing. Look for video walkthroughs and a real online presence. Red flag 4: slow responses. Expect a reply within about 30 minutes during the day, which is easier with a team behind the agent.

faq.q: How do I find the best real estate agent in the Twin Cities?
faq.a: Check Google and Zillow reviews (look for 50-plus), recent sales in your area and property type, how they market homes (video walkthroughs, online presence) and how quickly they respond.

faq.q: How many homes does the average real estate agent sell?
faq.a: About five a year, according to the video. Agents on the Huerkamp Home Group team average about 17.

takeaways: A snowy tour of a Country Joe Homes twin home in the Autumn Hills neighborhood of Lakeville, one of the builder's hottest-selling products at the time, priced in the mid-$500,000s.

It's a rambler-style twin home with one-level living: about 2,000 square feet above grade, two bedrooms and two baths, a wide entry, a flex room or second bedroom, a large kitchen island seating four or five and laundry connected to the owner's closet.
The owner's suite has a mini-vaulted ceiling, a dual vanity, a soaking tub and a large walk-in closet.
The unfinished basement could nearly double the space, with room for bedrooms, a family room and a bath (already plumbed). Jason estimates about $75,000 to $100,000 to finish it.
Country Joe is a family-owned builder that has built in Lakeville and the south and east metro for decades.

faq.q: Are there one-level twin homes in Lakeville?
faq.a: Yes. Country Joe Homes builds rambler-style twin homes in Lakeville's Autumn Hills, with the owner's suite, laundry and living areas on the main floor.

takeaways: A tour of D.R. Horton's Elm plan in Whispering Fields in Farmington, on the east edge of Lakeville, where about 82 lots and several move-in-ready homes were available at the time.

About 2,400 square feet with a main-floor bedroom and three-quarter bath, an open kitchen with an island, and upstairs a loft, laundry, three bedrooms and an owner's suite on the opposite side of the house.
The model is slab-on-grade; a basement adds about $40,000 unfinished and roughly 1,000 more finishable square feet where the lot allows.

A move-in-ready Elm on a pond with a walkout basement and five bedrooms was priced at $519,000 at the time. Homes come with sod, two trees, irrigation, a tankless water heater and an air exchanger, and the neighborhood has walking paths and a playground.
Builder incentives were strong at the time; ask what's currently offered.

faq.q: What does about $520,000 buy in new construction in Farmington?
faq.a: In this tour, a move-in-ready D.R. Horton home of about 2,400 square feet with five bedrooms, a main-floor bedroom, a pond view and an unfinished walkout basement.

takeaways: A tour of Bridle Creek, a 95-home new-construction community in Jordan in the southwest metro, with 58 lots available at the time, a community pool and a club room, and easy access to Highway 169.

One model of about 2,500 square feet had five bedrooms (including a main-floor bedroom with a three-quarter bath) and three and a half baths, priced around $467,000 at the time, backing up to farm fields.
The Pine plan of about 2,000 square feet had four bedrooms upstairs, two and a half baths and an unfinished lookout basement with egress windows and bath rough-in, priced around $440,000.
Homes come with sod, irrigation, smart-home features, a tankless water heater, an air exchanger, a sump pump and a passive radon system. Jordan offers a small-town feel minutes from farmland.

faq.q: What does new construction cost in Jordan, Minnesota?
faq.a: In this Bridle Creek tour, new homes ran from about $440,000 for a four-bedroom, 2,000-square-foot plan to about $467,000 for a five-bedroom, 2,500-square-foot plan.

faq.q: Do new homes in Minnesota come with radon systems?
faq.a: Many do. The homes in this Jordan community include a passive radon system, which can be upgraded to an active system if testing shows it's needed.
